It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}, and under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank}} it was classified as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}. It is also known as “Anaori-no-miya Ikeda Shrine.” {{nihongo|'''Ikeda Shrine'''|伊居太神社 (池田市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Settsu Province]].

== History ==
During the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, {{ill|Achi no Omi|de|Achi no Omi|ja|阿知使主|zh|阿知使主|qid=Q11657596}} and {{ill|Tsuga no Omi|ja|都加使主|qid=Q24863564}}, a father and son who were dispatched to the state of {{ill|Northern and Southern dynasties|Q49696|qid=Q49696|lt=Wu}} (referring to the {{ill|Northern and Southern dynasties|Q49696|qid=Q49696|lt=Southern Dynasties}} of {{ill|China (region)|Q29520|qid=Q29520}}<ref>{{Cite news|author={{ill|Masatoshi Ishii|Q11585005|qid=Q11585005}}|date=2005-06|title=Japan–Korea Relations in the 5th Century – The Five Kings of Wa and Goguryeo and Baekje –|publisher={{ill|Japan–South Korea Joint History Research Project|Q11510754|qid=Q11510754}}|newspaper=Japan–Korea Joint History Research Report (Phase 1)|url=http://www.jkcf.or.jp/history_arch/first/1/1-03-ishii_j.pdf|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20151018092747/http://www.jkcf.or.jp/history_arch/first/1/1-03-ishii_j.pdf|archivedate=2015-10-18|page=147}}</ref>), in order to acquire weaving and sewing techniques, returned after requesting from the King of Wu four seamstresses: {{ill|Kurehatori|Q55525775|qid=Q55525775}}, {{ill|Anaori|Q119380538|qid=Q119380538}}, {{ill|Ehime|Q119380627|qid=Q119380627}}, and {{ill|Otohime|Q119380628|qid=Q119380628}}. Of these, the younger sister Anaori-hime of the Kureori and Anaori sisters, who had been welcomed to the Ikeda area, died in {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ar|الإمبراطور نينتوكو|arz|الامبراطور نينتوكو|azb|نینتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট নিন্তকু|br|Impalaer Nintoku|ca|Emperador Nintoku|cs|Nintoku|de|Nintoku|es|Nintoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور نینتوکو|fi|Nintoku|fr|Nintoku|hr|Nintoku|hu|Nintoku japán császár|id|Kaisar Nintoku|it|Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|ka|ნინტოკუ|ko|닌토쿠 천황|lt|Imperatorius Nintoku|ms|Maharaja Nintoku|nds|Nintoku|nl|Nintoku|pl|Nintoku|pt|Nintoku|ru|Император Нинтоку|sh|Car Nintoku|simple|Emperor Nintoku|sl|Cesar Nintoku|sv|Nintoku|th|จักรพรรดินินโตกุ|tl|Emperador Nintoku|tr|Nintoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Нінтоку|uz|Imperator Nintoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Nintoku|yo|Emperor Nintoku|zh|仁德天皇|zh_min_nan|Nintoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|仁德天皇|qid=Q313119}}’s 76th year, and it is said that she was enshrined the following year, in the 77th year, by Emperor Nintoku.

It is considered one of the candidate shrines (ronsha) for the Ikeda Shrine of {{ill|Kawabe District, Hyōgo|ceb|Kawanabe-gun|es|Distrito de Kawabe|fr|District de Kawabe|id|Distrik Kawabe, Hyōgo|it|Distretto di Kawabe|ja|川辺郡|ko|가와베군|pl|Powiat Kawabe|ru|Кавабе (уезд, Хёго)|zh|川邊郡|qid=Q1042053|lt=Kawabe District}} in {{ill|Settsu Province|ca|Província de Settsu|cs|Provincie Seccu|de|Provinz Settsu|eo|Provinco Seccu|es|Provincia de Settsu|fa|ولایت ستسو|fr|Province de Settsu|gl|Provincia de Settsu|hak|Settsu-koet|id|Provinsi Settsu|it|Settsu (provincia)|ja|摂津国|ko|셋쓰국|lt|Seccu žemė|nl|Settsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Settsu|ru|Сэтцу (провинция)|simple|Settsu Province|sk|Seccu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Сецу|tr|Settsu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Сеццу|zh|攝津國|zh_min_nan|Settu-kok|zh_yue|攝津國|qid=Q864163}} listed in the '{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}}'. The other candidate shrine is {{ill|Ikota Shrine|Q11379327|qid=Q11379327|lt=Ikeda Shrine}} (Ikota Shrine) in {{ill|Amagasaki|Q213318|qid=Q213318}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}.

In {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 4 ({{ill|785|Q30554|qid=Q30554}}), by imperial order of {{ill|Emperor Kanmu|Q314846|qid=Q314846}}, the shrine buildings were newly constructed, and Emperor Ōjin and Emperor Nintoku also came to be enshrined.

In {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 7 ({{ill|1579|Q6709|qid=Q6709}}), the shrine buildings were destroyed by fire in the warfare between {{ill|Oda Nobunaga|Q171411|qid=Q171411}} and {{ill|Araki Murashige|Q2859472|qid=Q2859472}} during the {{ill|Siege of Itami (1579)|Q7510108|qid=Q7510108}}. Later, in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 9 ({{ill|1604|Q6738|qid=Q6738}}), the main hall was rebuilt by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyori|Q313641|qid=Q313641}}.

In the {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} period, it was ranked as a {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

== Enshrined deities ==
* Principal deities – Anaori Daimyōjin, {{ill|Emperor Ōjin|Q317997|qid=Q317997}}, {{ill|Emperor Nintoku|ar|الإمبراطور نينتوكو|arz|الامبراطور نينتوكو|azb|نینتوکو (ایمپیراتور)|bn|সম্রাট নিন্তকু|br|Impalaer Nintoku|ca|Emperador Nintoku|cs|Nintoku|de|Nintoku|es|Nintoku Tennō|fa|امپراتور نینتوکو|fi|Nintoku|fr|Nintoku|hr|Nintoku|hu|Nintoku japán császár|id|Kaisar Nintoku|it|Nintoku|ja|仁徳天皇|ka|ნინტოკუ|ko|닌토쿠 천황|lt|Imperatorius Nintoku|ms|Maharaja Nintoku|nds|Nintoku|nl|Nintoku|pl|Nintoku|pt|Nintoku|ru|Император Нинтоку|sh|Car Nintoku|simple|Emperor Nintoku|sl|Cesar Nintoku|sv|Nintoku|th|จักรพรรดินินโตกุ|tl|Emperador Nintoku|tr|Nintoku (imparator)|uk|Імператор Нінтоку|uz|Imperator Nintoku|vi|Thiên hoàng Nintoku|yo|Emperor Nintoku|zh|仁德天皇|zh_min_nan|Nintoku Thian-hông|zh_yue|仁德天皇|qid=Q313119}}

== Shrine grounds ==
* Main hall – Rebuilt in {{ill|Keichō|Q1328185|qid=Q1328185}} 9 ({{ill|1604|Q6738|qid=Q6738}}) by {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyori|Q313641|qid=Q313641}}. It is the only example in Japan of a three-shrine (sansha-zukuri) structure with a chidori karahafu hipped roof.
* Middle gate
* Worship hall
* Yorimitsu Pine – A pine tree planted by {{ill|Minamoto no Yorimitsu|Q590523|qid=Q590523}}.
* Himemuro mound
* Shrine office
* Shrine gate

== Other ==
* Triangular-rimmed deity-and-beast mirror
*: A mirror handed down as a treasure of Ikeda Shrine. It is said to be a Chinese-made mirror and measures 20.5 centimeters in diameter. It is said to have been unearthed from Yokoyama (Yokikiyama) during the {{ill|Kyōwa|Q960763|qid=Q960763}} era ({{ill|1801|Q6877|qid=Q6877}}–{{ill|1803|Q6887|qid=Q6887}}), but the specific site of excavation (tumulus) is not known<ref>“Newly Revised History of Ikeda City, Vol. 1 (Geography, Archaeology, Ancient and Medieval History),” Ikeda City, 1997, pp. 187–188.</ref>.

== Other ==
* Also written as “Anaori-hime” or “Ayaori-hime.”
* “Ayaori-hime” is the origin of the town name “Aya” in {{ill|Ikeda, Osaka|ar|إكيدا (أوساكا)|arz|ايكيدا, اوساكا|ca|Ikeda (Osaka)|ce|Икеда (Осака)|ceb|Ikeda Shi|cy|Ikeda, Osaka|de|Ikeda (Osaka)|eo|Ikeda (Osaka)|es|Ikeda (Osaka)|et|Ikeda|fa|ایکه‌دا، اوساکا|fi|Ikeda (Osaka)|fr|Ikeda|gl|Ikeda, Ōsaka|it|Ikeda (Osaka)|ja|池田市|ko|이케다시|ms|Ikeda|mzn|ایکه‌دا، اوساکا|nl|Ikeda|no|Ikeda|pl|Ikeda (Osaka)|pt|Ikeda|ro|Ikeda, Osaka|ru|Икеда (Осака)|sh|Ikeda|sr|Икеда|sv|Ikeda, Ōsaka|szl|Ikeda|tg|Икеда|th|อิเกดะ (จังหวัดโอซากะ)|tl|Ikeda, Osaka|tr|Ikeda, Osaka|tt|Икеда (Осака)|uk|Ікеда (Осака)|ur|اکیڈا، اوساکا|vi|Ikeda, Ōsaka|war|Ikeda, Osaka|zh|池田市|zh_classical|池田市|zh_min_nan|Ikeda-chhī|zh_yue|池田|qid=Q817965}}.
* It is located right next to {{ill|Satsukiyama-park|Q11372461|qid=Q11372461}} and {{ill|Satsukiyama Zoo|Q11551834|qid=Q11551834|lt=Satsukiyama Zoo}}, forming an almost continuous area.
* It is the oldest extant {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Ikeda City.
* While Gofuku-hime is enshrined at {{ill|Kureha Shrine|Q11416775|qid=Q11416775}}, located on the {{ill|Ikeda Station (Osaka)|Q866156|qid=Q866156|lt=Ikeda Station}} side and regarded as the “Lower Shrine,” Ikeda Shrine at the foot of {{ill|Mount Satsuki|Q11372460|qid=Q11372460}} is regarded as the “Upper Shrine,” and the relationship between the two is very close.
* Locally, it is sometimes called “Ikota” Shrine.

== Access ==
* 15-minute walk from {{ill|Hankyu Takarazuka Main Line|Q3832859|qid=Q3832859|lt=Hankyu Takarazuka Line}} / {{ill|Ikeda Station (Osaka)|Q866156|qid=Q866156|lt=Ikeda Station}}.
* 5-minute walk from Aya Town via {{ill|Hankyu Bus|Q11656745|qid=Q11656745}}.
